_note: expected_problem is the LAB's own plain-English label, used only to explain the before column. It is never sent to the product. Thresholds are industry-typical guesses, not any publisher's spec sheet.

fixtures.expected_problem: This ad is 45 seconds; the slot is 30 seconds.
Uses VAST 2.0; streaming TV needs VAST 4.x.
Picture is 640x480; streaming TV needs widescreen HD.
Audio bitrate is 64 kbps; minimum is 128 kbps.
Size 300x600 is not one of the planned sizes (300x250, 728x90).
The ad does not say how long it is, so nobody can check it fits the slot.

cases.title: Seven ads, six with a problem
cases.description: One good streaming TV ad plus six that each break one rule: too long, old VAST version, wrong picture size, low audio quality, wrong banner size, and no duration declared.
cases.expect_after: The campaign is held back from launch, every broken ad is marked invalid with a plain-English reason, and the good ad is marked valid.

cases.title: The headline case: three streaming TV ads
cases.description: One good 30-second ad, one 45-second ad for a 30-second slot, and one built on the outdated VAST 2.0 standard.
cases.expect_after: The campaign is held back from launch, every broken ad is marked invalid with a plain-English reason, and the good ad is marked valid.

cases.title: Only good ads: one per channel
cases.description: A good streaming TV ad, a good display banner and a good radio spot. Nothing is wrong, so the check must not get in the way.
cases.expect_after: All three ads are marked valid and the campaign reaches READY (the check must not block good campaigns).
